articles.text: MĚIGUÓ XUÉZHĚ: Měicì lái Zhōngguó zǒngshi yào máfan ni, péizhe wǒmen pǎolái pǎoqù. Nǐ shénme shíhou yě dào Měiguó qù kànkan ma! Sān-sìshínián le, Měiguó yǐjīng biànde tài duō le!
AMERICAN SCHOLAR: Every time I come to China I always trouble you to accompany us all around the place. You should really come see America some time! It's changed a lot in thirty or forty years!
ZHŌNGGUÓ PÉNGYOU: Shì a! Qù shi hěn xiǎng qùde, zhǐ shi yìshí hái zhǎobudào jīhui.
CHINESE FRIEND: Yes, I'd love to go, it's just that for the moment I can't find the opportunity.
MĚIGUÓ XUÉZHĚ: Gēlúnbǐyà Dàxué cháng qǐng tāmende lǎo xuésheng huíqu cānguān, yóulǎn. Wǒ shìshi gěi ni ānpái yíxiàr.
AMERICAN SCHOLAR: Columbia University often invites their old students back to visit and tour. I'll try to arrange it for you.

ZHŌNGGUÓ PÉNGYOU: Hǎode.... Shuōqilai yě qíguài, Niǔ Yuē zhēn ge tèbiéde dìfang. Wǒ zhù zài nàrde shíhou bù juéde zěnme tài hǎo, kěshi xiànzài cháng xiǎngqǐ ta! Yǒu hěn duō lǎo liúxuéshēng cháng shuō, shéi zài Niǔ Yuē zhùguo, shéi jiù huì chángcháng xiǎngzhe ta!

CHINESE FRIEND: Okay.... It's a funny thing, but New York is really a special place. When I was living there, I didn't think much of the place, but now I often think of it. A lot of old students returned from abroad often say that whoever has lived in New York will think of it often!
MĚIGUÓ XUÉZHĚ: Ō, wǒmen bù tán zhèige le. Zài tánxiaqu wǒ yě yào xiǎng jiā le. Wǒmen háishi chūqu zǒuzou ba!
AMERICAN SCHOLAR: Let's not talk about this any more. If we keep talking about it, I'm going to start missing home, too. It would be better if we went outside for a walk!
ZHŌNGGUÓ PÉNGYOU: Hǎo a! Nǐ xiǎng qù nǎr a?
CHINESE FRIEND: All right! Where would you like to go?
MĚIGUÓ XUÉZHĚ: Běijīng shi shǒudū, yídìng yǒu xiē yǒu yìside dìfang. Gùgōng, Yíhéyuán shénmede wǒ dōu qùguo le. Fùjìn hái yǒu shénme biéde dìfang bǐjiào yǒu yìsi ma?
AMERICAN SCHOLAR: Běijīng is the capital, so it naturally has some interesting places. I've been to the Palace Museum and the Summer Palace. Are there any other interesting places near here?
ZHŌNGGUÓ PÉNGYOU: Cóng zhèli chūqu wǎng xī zǒu, chuānguò Tiān'ānmén Guǎngchǎng, zài Tiān'ānménde xībianr yǒu yíge gōngyuánr, jiào Zhōngshān Gōngyuán, lǐmian yǒu bù shǎo piàoliangde gǔdài jiànzhù.

CHINESE FRIEND: If you go out from here and walk to the west, then cut across Tiān'ānmén Square, then on the west side of Tiān'ānmén there's a park called Sun Yatsen Park, and inside there are a lot of beautiful ancient buildings.
MĚIGUÓ XUÉZHĚ: Shi shénme cháodàide jiànzhù, yǒu duōshǎo niánde lìshǐ le?
AMERICAN SCHOLAR: What dynasty are the buildings from? How old are they?
ZHŌNGGUÓ PÉNGYOU: Zuì zǎode jiànzhù shi Liáodàide, chàbuduō yǒu yìqiānniánde lìshǐ le. Nàr hái yǒu qīkē gǔdàide dà shù, yě dōu yǒu yìqiānduō nián le.
CHINESE FRIEND: The earliest buildings are from the Liáo Period. They are about a thousand years old. There are also seven ancient trees there, which are over a thousand years old, too.
MĚIGUÓ XUÉZHĚ: Nàr yě yǒu yǒu míngde gōngdiàn ba?
AMERICAN SCHOLAR: There's a famous palace there too, isn't there?
ZHŌNGGUÓ PÉNGYOU: Ōu, yǒu yízuò dà diàn shi Míngcháode shíhour jiànzhùde, yòngde cáiliào quán shi mùtou, yě yǐjīng chàbuduō yǒu liùbǎiniánde lìshǐ.
CHINESE FRIEND: Yes. There's a large palace which was constructed in the Míng Dynasty, made entirely of wood. That's about six hundred years old, too.
MĚIGUÓ XUÉZHĚ: Hǎo, nà wǒmen xiànzài jiù qù zǒuzou.
AMERICAN SCHOLAR: All right, then let's go for a walk right now.
ZHŌNGGUÓ PÉNGYOU: Hǎode, zǒu!
CHINESE FRIEND: Okay, let's go!
